<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I need to understand what happens when the headset disconnects - does hid.read block forever or return empty?

Checking the hidapi Python bindings to see how disconnects are handled.

Checking if hid.read blocks indefinitely without a timeout. The USB dongle may remain present after headset disconnect, so the indicator must detect actual connection loss. A timeout on reads is needed so the loop can check timestamps and trigger flashing.

A watchdog thread could monitor packet timestamps instead of relying solely on read timeouts. The plan tracks connection state: first valid EEG packet marks the headset as ever connected, and a timeout without valid packets triggers the disconnected state. A callback will toggle the tray icon between normal and dimmed or blank states. Icon assets must be bundled with PyInstaller, and a resource path helper is needed for frozen executables. The indicator should remain silent on startup and only flash after the first successful connection is lost.

The thread must not crash on initial device discovery failure. Reconnect logic is out of scope. The flashing will alternate between the normal icon and a dimmed, blank, or red-tinted variant.

A red-tinted alert icon will be generated at runtime from the normal icon using PIL, avoiding a second asset file. The disconnect threshold is set to three seconds without valid EEG packets. The hid.read call will use a one-second timeout so the loop can periodically check for disconnection.

An OSError raised by hid.read when the dongle is unplugged will also be treated as a disconnect, provided the headset was ever connected.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I have a solid plan. One decision: should flashing continue until reconnect, and should we detect reconnect?

The flashing indicator should stop once the headset reconnects.

Reconnect detection is needed to restore the tray icon. HID reads must use a timeout because the dongle may keep returning empty data when the headset is off. The hidapi Python binding supports this.

Empty HID reads after a timeout will signal a lost connection. The plan adds a connection-change callback, tracks ever-connected and currently-connected states, and drives the tray flash timer from a background thread or the Emotiv thread with locking.

pystray icon and title updates from another thread are safe on Windows with the win32 backend. A dedicated flash thread will toggle the icon whenever the `disconnected_alert` flag is set. For the frozen executable, resource paths must use `sys._MEIPASS` because recent PyInstaller onedir versions place bundled data inside `_internal`.

The bundled icon will be added to the PyInstaller datas list. A three-second HID timeout is chosen as a sensible default. The tray will alternate between the normal icon and a red-tinted version. Flashing is suppressed until the first successful connection. Reconnect detection is limited to stopping the flash when packets resume.

The Emotiv thread must catch exceptions around the main loop. If the HID device is unplugged and the read throws, the disconnected callback must fire before the thread dies. Otherwise the tray would keep flashing forever. If the thread crashes before that callback, the alert stays off. A failed initial HID open is also acceptable because the flash is suppressed until the first successful connection.

The alert will trigger on lost EEG packet flow rather than on USB dongle presence, since the dongle can be present without the headset actually connected. The requirements are clear enough to proceed without further questions.
</details></think>

  "plan": "# Flashing tray indicator for headset disconnect\n\n## Behavior\n\n- **Connected**: first valid 14-channel EEG sample pushed in [`emotiv_lsl/emotiv_base.py`](c:\\Users\\pho\\repos\\EmotivEpoc\\ACTIVE_DEV\\emotiv-lsl\\emotiv_lsl\\emotiv_base.py) `main_loop()`.\n- **Disconnected (alert)**: after that first success, no valid EEG for **3 seconds**, or HID read raises (dongle unplugged / device error).\n- **Before first connect**: tray stays normal (no flash), even if startup fails or headset is missing.\n- **On EEG resume**: stop flashing and restore the normal icon/tooltip.\n- Flash: ~500 ms toggle between the normal icon and a red-tinted copy (generated with Pillow at runtime).         def _mark_eeg_received() -> None:
            nonlocal ever_connected, is_connected, last_eeg_time
            last_eeg_time = time.monotonic()
            if not is_connected:
                was_ever = ever_connected
                ever_connected = True
                is_connected = True
                logger.info("Headset EEG connection established" if not was_ever else "Headset EEG connection restored")
                self._notify_connection_change(True)

        def _mark_disconnected(reason: str) -> None:
            nonlocal is_connected
            if ever_connected and is_connected:
                is_connected = False
                logger.warning(f"Headset EEG connection lost ({reason})")
                self._notify_connection_change(False)
